pharm: Oral selective inhibitor of JAK1 and JAK2 tyrosine kinases, blocking cytokine and growth factor signaling involved in hematopoiesis and immune function
quick: Myelofibrosis: 20 mg PO BID if platelets >200,000; titrate by platelet count
May be taken with or without food
Avoid; may cause fetal harm based on animal data
Do not breastfeed during and for 2 weeks after the last dose
Reduce dose in moderate/severe impairment and ESRD by platelet count
Reduce dose in hepatic impairment by platelet count (Child-Pugh)
No specific interaction established; use sensibly
CBC every 2-4 weeks until stable; infection and lipid surveillance
summary: Ruxolitinib is an oral inhibitor of Janus kinases JAK1 and JAK2 used to treat intermediate or high-risk myelofibrosis, polycythemia vera intolerant of or refractory to hydroxyurea, and steroid-refractory acute or chronic graft-versus-host disease. By blocking JAK-STAT signaling it reduces splenomegaly, constitutional symptoms, and pathologic blood counts. Dosing is individualized to platelet count, and the principal hazards reflect the JAK inhibitor class: dose-dependent cytopenias, serious infections, thrombosis, major adverse cardiovascular events, and malignancy.
indications: Intermediate or high-risk myelofibrosis, including primary myelofibrosis, post-polycythemia vera myelofibrosis, and post-essential thrombocythemia myelofibrosis, in adults
Polycythemia vera in adults with inadequate response to or intolerance of hydroxyurea
Steroid-refractory acute graft-versus-host disease in adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older
Chronic graft-versus-host disease after failure of one or two lines of systemic therapy in adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older

dosage.t: With or without food; titrate based on response and platelet count
dosage.n: Maximum 25 mg twice daily during titration
Use caution; hold if platelets fall below 50 x 10^9/L

dosage.t: With or without food; titrate to hematocrit control
dosage.n: Adjust based on response and tolerability
May increase to 10 mg twice daily if counts permit

admin: Administer orally twice daily at approximately the same times each day
May be taken with or without food
Obtain a complete blood count before starting and every 2 to 4 weeks until doses are stabilized, then as clinically indicated
Reduce dose by 50% with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or with fluconazole at doses up to 200 mg daily
Modify or interrupt dosing for thrombocytopenia, anemia, and neutropenia per platelet and count thresholds
When stopping, taper gradually (for example by 5 mg twice daily each week) rather than discontinuing abruptly, except for life-threatening toxicity
moa: Ruxolitinib inhibits Janus-associated kinases JAK1 and JAK2, which mediate the signaling of a number of cytokines and growth factors important for hematopoiesis and immune function. JAK signaling activates STAT transcription factors. In myeloproliferative neoplasms, dysregulated JAK1/JAK2 signaling (including via JAK2 V617F mutations) drives excess proliferation and constitutional symptoms; ruxolitinib blocks this signaling, reducing splenomegaly, symptom burden, and overactive blood cell production.

relative: History of major adverse cardiovascular events or thrombosis (caution; class warning)
monitor: Signs of infection including TB and viral reactivation
Skin examination for non-melanoma skin cancer

preg: Based on findings in animal studies, ruxolitinib may cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman. There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Avoid use in pregnancy; if used, advise the patient of the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: There are no data on the presence of ruxolitinib in human milk or its effects on the breastfed infant or on milk production. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in the breastfed child, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for two weeks after the final dose.
renal: In moderate or severe renal impairment, no dose adjustment is needed for myelofibrosis if platelets are above 150 x 10^9/L; for platelets 100 to 150 x 10^9/L give 10 mg twice daily, and for platelets 50 to less than 100 x 10^9/L give 5 mg once daily (avoid use if platelets are below 50 x 10^9/L). In ESRD on dialysis with myelofibrosis, give a single dose after dialysis of 15 mg (platelets 100-200 x 10^9/L) or 20 mg (platelets above 200 x 10^9/L); for polycythemia vera on dialysis give 10 mg once after dialysis. Do not use the extended-release formulation in renal impairment.
hepatic: For myelofibrosis with hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh A, B, or C), no adjustment is needed if platelets exceed 150 x 10^9/L; give 10 mg twice daily for platelets 100 to 150 x 10^9/L and 5 mg once daily for platelets 50 to less than 100 x 10^9/L. For polycythemia vera with hepatic impairment, give 5 mg twice daily across severity classes. Monitor blood counts more closely.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin) - reduce ruxolitinib dose by 50%
Fluconazole (a combined CYP3A4/CYP2C9 inhibitor) at doses up to 200 mg daily - reduce dose by 50%; avoid fluconazole doses greater than 200 mg daily
moderate: Strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin) may reduce ruxolitinib exposure; monitor response and consider dose adjustment
Other myelosuppressive agents may increase the risk of cytopenias
minor: Mild or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors generally do not require routine dose adjustment but warrant monitoring
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; food does not require dose adjustment
interactions.alcohol: No specific clinically significant interaction with alcohol is established
interactions.diagnostics: Screen for tuberculosis and viral hepatitis before therapy; monitor complete blood counts and lipid panels during treatment

serious: Serious bacterial, mycobacterial, fungal, and viral infections (including tuberculosis)
Thrombosis (deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, arterial thrombosis)
Secondary malignancies including non-melanoma skin cancer and lymphoma
rare: Herpes zoster reactivation with serious complications
emergency: Signs of serious infection or sepsis (high fever, rigors)
Symptoms of stroke or myocardial infarction
Sudden shortness of breath, chest pain, or limb swelling suggesting thrombosis
Acute febrile illness with cytopenias after discontinuation (symptom flare) - seek urgent care

monitoring: Complete blood count before starting, then every 2 to 4 weeks until doses are stabilized, then as clinically indicated
Platelet count to guide dosing and dose modification
Screening for tuberculosis and active infection before and during therapy
Hepatitis B status and viral reactivation in at-risk patients
Lipid parameters about 8 to 12 weeks after starting
Periodic skin examination for non-melanoma skin cancer
Cardiovascular and thromboembolic risk and symptoms
counsel: Take exactly as prescribed, twice daily, with or without food; do not stop suddenly without talking to your clinician
You will need regular blood tests to check blood counts and adjust the dose
Report fever, chills, cough, or any sign of infection promptly, including shingles or unusual rashes
Seek immediate care for chest pain, sudden weakness or trouble speaking, or sudden leg swelling or breathlessness
Tell your clinician about all medicines, especially antifungals like fluconazole or ketoconazole, which require a dose reduction
Use effective contraception and do not breastfeed during treatment and for two weeks after the last dose
pk: Spleen size and symptom reductions develop over the first weeks of therapy
Maximum plasma concentration reached approximately 1 to 2 hours after an oral dose
Mean elimination half-life approximately 3 hours (active metabolites about 5.8 hours)
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); excursions permitted 15-30 C (59-86 F)
pearls: Starting dose is set by platelet count in myelofibrosis (20 mg BID if >200,000, 15 mg BID if 100,000-200,000, 5 mg BID if 50,000 to <100,000)
Dose-dependent thrombocytopenia and anemia are expected; manage with dose reduction or interruption rather than abrupt stoppage
Reduce dose by 50% with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or fluconazole up to 200 mg/day; avoid higher fluconazole doses
Carries JAK inhibitor class concerns: serious infections (including TB and PML), MACE, thrombosis, and secondary malignancies
Abrupt discontinuation can trigger a symptom flare resembling acute illness; taper gradually when stopping
missed: If a dose is missed, do not take an extra dose; take the next prescribed dose at the usual scheduled time. Do not double up to make up for a missed dose, and do not stop or interrupt therapy on your own without consulting the prescriber, because abrupt discontinuation can cause a flare of disease symptoms.
overdose: There is no specific antidote for ruxolitinib overdose. Single doses up to 200 mg have been given with acceptable acute tolerability, while repeated higher-than-recommended doses are associated with increased myelosuppression including leukopenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia. Management is supportive; hemodialysis is not expected to enhance elimination of ruxolitinib. Monitor blood counts closely and treat cytopenias and any complications.
